The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3D process is a promising technology to achieve a low material budget, while the INMAPS process is very attractive for the possibility to implement the 2D architecture and the high resistive epitaxial layer.

the 3D technology allows the production of sensors with a material budget of less than 0.1% X0 per layer, with excellent performance, while the INMAPS process is promising for the development of 2D MAPs with a material budget below 0.2% X0.

the 3D integration process can be used to build high resolution sensors with very low material budget and low leakage currents, while the INMAPS process allows for a further reduction of the material budget and the leakage currents.
